newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks sink on worries of cool-down moves.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks sink on worries of cool-down moves.

text.p: With volume surging toward historic levels, Taiwan share prices suffered their first loss in more than a week on Wednesday, dogged by worries of possible official actions to cool the red-hot bourse, brokers said. Following seven straight days of rises, the benchmark stock index spurted to an early high of 8,599.52 before turning lower. It closed down 84.68 points or 0.99 percent at 8,441.52.
Turnover was a huge T$195.7 billion -- the highest in more than seven years -- as investors dumped shares to lock in profits, brokers said.
The government's apparent new resolve to restrain unapproved Taiwan investment in China also discouraged investors, giving a handy excuse for profit-taking, brokers said.
But fear of administrative actions were the top worry.

"Reported plans by the government to cool down the bourse weakened market sentiment. Investors also were discouraged by the central bank action to repeatedly mop up excess funds," said George Hou, fund manager of Jardine Fleming.
The central bank was issuing T$10 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit on Wednesday, the latest in a series of issues to tighten up loose liquidity.
Many experts say easy money, not industrial fundamentals, has been the main force behind Taiwan's dramatic stock rise.
Electronics were hardest hit, losing 3.01 percent on profit taking against strong recent performance as well as concern over falling world prices for high-tech products, brokers said.

Footwear maker Pou Chen, which reportedly is financing a Shanghai bank without Taiwan approval, tumbled 5.5 percent or T$7.0 to T$120.5 on a government warning that unauthorised China investments would be punished.
